SHOPIFY ACCESSIBILITY EVIDENCE

Turn an axe scan into a record you can review.

Paste an axe-core JSON export to get a dated summary of violations, passes, and items needing review. Nothing leaves this browser. Need a price? Estimate remediation hours and a quote range from the same scan. Need to know which Liquid file to open? Route the scan to likely theme areas. Need to see what a fix changed? Compare before and after scans. Wondering how this differs from a paid widget? See this tool vs. accessiBe. Formatting a government website scan for ADA Title II? The ADA Title II evidence report turns the same kind of axe-core JSON into a dated Title II record with a WCAG 2.1 AA split.

Paste axe JSON

Evidence record

No report generated yet.
Your report will appear here.

Common questions

Does this evidence record prove my Shopify store is ADA/WCAG compliant?

No. It formats whatever axe-core found into a dated, readable record — it does not run a scan itself, does not check anything axe-core cannot detect (like actual screen-reader usability or keyboard-trap edge cases), and does not determine legal compliance. Treat it as documentation of one automated test at one point in time, not a compliance certificate.

Where do I get the axe JSON to paste in?

Run axe-core (the axe DevTools browser extension, axe-core CLI, or a similar tool) against your storefront and export its JSON results — this page only formats output you already generated elsewhere, it does not crawl or scan your site itself.

Does my scan data get uploaded anywhere?

No. The JSON you paste is parsed and formatted entirely in your browser; nothing is sent to a server. Usage counting only tallies anonymous feature events in localStorage, with an opt-out checkbox above.

What's the difference between this and the quote or theme-areas tools?

This page turns a scan into a readable evidence record; the quote tool estimates remediation hours and a price range from the same JSON; theme-areas maps violations to likely Liquid template files to open; and the comparison tool diffs two scans to show what a fix actually changed. They all run on the same axe export, just answering different questions about it.

vs-accessibe.html.text:
← Shopify Accessibility Evidence Report

This tool vs. accessiBe

Two different shapes: accessiBe installs an ongoing widget and audit subscription on your live storefront. This page formats an axe-core scan you already ran into a dated, portable evidence record, free and local — no widget, no installation, nothing shipped to your customers.

What each product is for

accessiBe sells accessWidget, a JavaScript widget installed on a live storefront that applies automated interface adjustments and AI-driven remediation aimed at WCAG conformance every time a visitor loads the page, alongside audits, a generated accessibility statement, and ongoing monitoring — described on accessiBe's own site as a paid, ongoing subscription product. It is built for a merchant who wants an installed layer running on the storefront itself, plus a vendor relationship for audits and monitoring over time. accessiBe's own current pricing and contract terms are not repeated here, since this session cannot verify today's figures against accessiBe's site; only its well-documented product shape — an installed widget plus an audit/monitoring subscription — is described.

This tool does none of what accessWidget does. It installs nothing on a storefront, changes nothing a customer sees, and has no ongoing subscription. It takes the axe-core JSON export you already generated somewhere else — the axe DevTools browser extension, the axe-core CLI, or a similar tool — and formats it into a dated, readable evidence record: violation count, affected nodes, passing rules, and items needing manual review. It runs entirely in your browser, needs no account and no site access, and uploads nothing you paste.

QuestionWhere to answer it
I want an installed layer that adjusts my live storefront's interface for visitors, on every page load, without a developer fixing the theme.accessiBe — that is the installed-widget job accessWidget is built for.
I already ran an axe-core scan and want a dated, readable record of what it found, to file or hand to a developer or client.This tool — paste the JSON, get the record, free and instant, nothing installed.
I want an ongoing vendor relationship: recurring audits, a generated accessibility statement, and monitoring over time.accessiBe or a comparable subscription service — this page has no memory between visits and no ongoing service.
I want to know exactly what my own axe-core scan found, without a widget layered on top changing what a screen reader or keyboard user actually encounters.This tool — it reports only what the scan you supply contains, nothing more and nothing injected onto the page.
Do I need to install anything on my storefront, or give the tool access to my site, to use it?This tool: no. accessWidget is installed directly on the storefront by design.

A merchant can reasonably want both: an installed widget and audit subscription like accessiBe's for the live storefront experience, and a free local tool like this one for turning a specific axe-core run into a record that outlives any single dashboard. This page does not evaluate accessWidget's effectiveness or make any claim about whether an installed overlay satisfies a legal obligation — it only describes accessiBe's documented product shape and states what this tool does differently.

This tool needs no account and no sign-in: it is a static page, the formatting runs in your browser, and once it has loaded it keeps working with the connection off.

Common questions

Should I use this tool or accessiBe?

They are different shapes of product. accessiBe sells accessWidget, a JavaScript widget installed on a live site that applies automated interface adjustments and AI-driven remediation aimed at WCAG conformance, plus audits, an accessibility statement, and ongoing monitoring — described on accessiBe's own site as a paid, ongoing subscription that runs on your storefront every time a visitor loads it. This page does none of that. It has no widget, installs nothing on your storefront, and changes nothing a customer sees. It takes an axe-core JSON export you already generated somewhere else and turns it into a dated, readable evidence record in your browser — violations, passes, and items needing review — that you can copy or download for a client file or a remediation ticket. A merchant who wants an installed layer that adjusts the live storefront on every visit, plus ongoing audits and a vendor accessibility statement, is buying a different product than a merchant who wants a free, private record of one automated test.

No. This site is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by accessiBe, Inc. accessiBe and accessWidget are trademarks of accessiBe, Inc., named here only to describe what this tool is and is not, based on accessiBe's own public site.

Common questions

How do I compare accessibility scans before and after a Shopify fix?

Export axe-core JSON from the same storefront URL before the change and after it. Paste the earlier export in Before and the later export in After, then choose Compare scans. The page lists rules that disappeared, rules that remain (with node-count change), and rules that appeared only in the later scan. That is a diff of two supplied results, not a compliance determination.

Does a resolved rule mean the storefront is compliant?

No. A resolved rule only means that rule id was in the earlier export and not in the later one. Manual review is still required. The comparison does not prove a fix was complete.

Is my axe JSON uploaded?

No. Both scans stay in your browser. The tool counts only anonymous feature events in localStorage, with an opt-out.
